plan.summary: This concise 5‑day study plan covers the core data‑visualization concepts from the course notes, including data preprocessing, string parsing, groupby aggregation, bar plots, heatmaps, regression plots, categorical visualizations, and interactive charts with Plotly and Cufflinks. Each day focuses on a specific theme and provides actionable tasks to reinforce learning within a 60‑minute study block.

tasks: Load the IPL 2022 dataset and inspect its shape and columns with df.info() and df.shape.
Check for missing values and convert the 'Best Bowling Figure' column from strings like '3--20' to integer wickets using lambda and .apply().
Group by 'Best Bowling' and compute the sum of 'Highest Wickets' to identify top wicket‑takers.
Use value_counts() on the 'Match Winner' column to get win counts per team.
Create a horizontal bar plot with Matplotlib’s plt.barh() to display team win totals.
Interpret the plot and note which team leads the season.
Calculate the correlation matrix of numeric columns with df.corr().
Plot a heatmap using Seaborn’s sns.heatmap() with annot=True to show exact correlation values.
Identify strong positive or negative relationships and consider their implications.
Generate a scatter plot with a regression line using sns.lmplot() for two continuous variables (e.g., total_bill vs. tip).
Adjust hue and markers to differentiate categories.
Interpret the slope and R² to understand the linear relationship.
Convert a static Matplotlib bar plot to an interactive Plotly chart using df.iplot() via Cufflinks.
Add hover information and enable zoom/pan features.
Export the interactive chart to an HTML file for sharing.

tips: Use a Jupyter notebook to combine code, visualizations, and markdown notes in one place.
After each task, write a brief reflection on what you learned and any questions that arise.
Keep a running log of the commands you run; this will help you reproduce results and debug later.
Schedule short breaks during the 60‑minute block to maintain focus.
Review the previous day’s work before starting a new topic to reinforce retention.

plan.summary: This 20‑day plan builds on the data‑visualization and pandas skills from the PDF to give you a solid foundation in machine learning. Each day you’ll spend one hour reviewing theory, coding key concepts, and applying them to small projects, progressing from data preprocessing to regression, classification, evaluation, and model deployment.

tasks: Read PDF sections on data cleaning and string parsing
Practice pandas .apply() and .astype() on a sample dataset
Write a short script to handle missing values
Explore feature extraction from text columns
Study the math behind least squares
Read seaborn lmplot example from PDF
Implement simple linear regression with sklearn
Add multiple features to the regression model
Implement logistic regression on a binary dataset
Apply cross_val_score to regression and classification
Compare models (LR vs. KNN vs. Decision Tree)
Build sklearn Pipeline with preprocessing and estimator
Apply Ridge and Lasso to regression
Train SVM for regression and classification
Create a simple Flask API for a trained model
Solve 3 practice problems on regression and classification
Take a timed practice quiz covering all topics
Prepare study notes for exam day

tips: Allocate 5‑minute warm‑up before coding to outline steps; use Jupyter notebooks for interactive experiments; keep a log of errors and fixes to reinforce learning; schedule short breaks during the hour to maintain focus; review PDF visual examples to solidify concepts.

plan.summary: The PDF offers a comprehensive narrative of Salah ad‑Din al‑Ayubi’s military and political achievements, centering on his decisive conquest of Edessa and its far‑reaching consequences for both Muslim and Christian realms. It details Zangi’s suppression of the Edessa conspiracy, the maturation of the Jihad movement, Crusader strategies and alliances with Western Europe, the Muslim response to Crusader incursions, and the pivotal siege of Alexandria. The text also touches on economic motivations of European merchants and the broader socio‑political context of the 12th‑13th centuries.

tasks: Read page 131 – note key events of the Edessa conspiracy and its suppression by Zangi
Summarize the political and military consequences of the conquest
Create flashcards for terms: Zangi, Edessa, Jihad, Crusader
Review the timeline of events from 1190‑1200
Read pages 33, 154, 66, 226, 43 – extract main points on colonialist influence, Crusader alliances, Alexandria siege, and economic motives
Draft a mind‑map linking Crusader strategies to Muslim responses
Identify and list key dates and figures mentioned
Rehearse the summary aloud to reinforce memory

tips: Use active recall by testing yourself on flashcard content after each reading session
Apply spaced repetition: review flashcards at increasing intervals (e.g., 1h, 4h, 24h)
Summarize each page in your own words to ensure comprehension
Create a timeline of events to visualize cause‑effect relationships
Stay hydrated and take short 5‑minute breaks to maintain focus
